title: Sign-Constrained Neural Processes for Transferring Probabilistic Fire Danger across Fujian, China
content: Danger ratings are built where fires have been recorded and used where they have not, so their value rests on how much of a fitted response survives a move to another landscape. We test that question on a benchmark assembled for Fujian province, southeast China, from 43,400 quality-filtered VIIRS and MODIS active-fire detections, daily reanalysis meteorology and terrain derivatives: 171 grid cells of 0.25°, 2922 days and 15,205 fire cell-days at a base rate of 3.04%. Models are fitted on the coastal belt and the lowland interior (2015–2019) and evaluated on the mountain interior in 2021–2022, a region absent from training. The model we propose keeps the response linear in standardized predictors, learns a prior over its coefficients from 24 source blocks, and constrains the humidity and wind coefficients by sign while training, which makes an increase of predicted probability with humidity, or a decrease with wind, unreachable for any input. On the held-out region it reaches an AUC-PR of 0.079 (95% interval 0.067–0.092), against 0.093 for logistic regression and 0.101 for a random forest, while its negative log-likelihood of 0.135 trails the best baseline at 0.123. Two consequences follow. Exact monotonicity is obtained at a measurable cost in sharpness, since every unconstrained model fails the wind test on 100.0% of matched pairs. Local labels do help as well: 256 labelled cell-days lift AUC-PR from 0.079 to 0.101, the same level a logistic regression reaches by refitting on those labels (0.103), so the closed-form update is a safe instrument, not a source of gain.
